facility_roles.quote: NA35 was the first experiment in the family of heavy-ion experiments conducted at the H2 beamline of the CERN North Area at the SPS.

facility_roles.note: Light-ion beams (p, d, 16O, 32S) from the SPS (accelerator:sps).
facility_roles.quote: NA35 recorded data on collisions of p, d, 16 O, and 32 S beams at 60A GeV/c and 200A GeV/c with S, Ag, and Au targets from 1986 to 1992.

intervals.label: proposal to the PS committee
intervals.note: The proposal (16O beams of 9-13A GeV at the PS) was submitted on 26 January 1982. The interval ends on the Greybook approval date (3 February 1983); CERN later moved the ion beams from the PS to the SPS.
intervals.quote: The origins of the NA35 experiment at CERN can be traced back to a proposal [1] submitted by the GSI–LBL–Heidelberg–Marburg–Warsaw Collaboration to CERN’s Proton Synchrotron and Synchro-Cyclotron Committee on January 26, 1982.

name: NA35
notes: Hall inferred: placed at the EHN1 site record because NA35 ran on the H2 beam line (Greybook: beam H2) and the NA61/SHINE Beams page says the H2 beam goes to Experimental Hall North 1; no fetched source names the NA35 hall directly (the same placement as NA49 and NA61/SHINE).
Major components of the detector were inherited from the NA5 and NA24 experiments (arXiv:2603.08053); those experiments are not Atlas records.
Successor: NA49 (the NA35 Collaboration initiated NA49 and NA49 replaced the streamer chamber by TPCs); the lineage row is on experiment:na49.

The Greybook approval date (3 February 1983) is the original PS approval; the SPS first-generation approval was in November 1984 (Specht slides; Greybook status row). The approval interval keeps the Greybook experiment-level date.
No membership, institution count or formation date was found; spokespersons per arXiv:2603.10835 were Reinhard Stock, then Peter Seyboth (Greybook lists Seyboth as spokesperson).

physics_goals.locator: NA35 official site (Internet Archive capture), main page
physics_goals.quote: Studies the stopping power of nuclear matter with different nuclear targets, and searches for evidence of formation of quark matter or quark-gluon plasma.
physics_goals.value: Study relativistic nucleus-nucleus collisions at the SPS: charged-particle multiplicity, proton and pion rapidity distributions, energy flow and strange-particle production, and search for quark matter or quark-gluon plasma

summary.plain: NA35 was one of the first CERN experiments to collide oxygen and sulphur nuclei at the SPS. Its streamer chamber photographed whole collisions and found that central sulphur-sulphur collisions produce many more strange particles than proton collisions, an early hint of quark-gluon plasma.
summary.technical: NA35: streamer chamber (200x120x70 cm3 sensitive volume, 1.5 T vertical field) with four downstream calorimeters on the H2 beam line of the SPS North Area; p, d, 16O and 32S beams at 60A and 200A GeV/c on S, Ag and Au targets, 1986-1992; observed enhanced neutral strange-hadron production in central S+S collisions at 200A GeV/c; two-pion correlations; its upgrade became NA49.

unique_capabilities.quote: The NA35 setup shown in Fig. 1 featured a visual tracking detector, a streamer chamber with a sensitive volume of 200×120×70 cm3 , placed in a 1.5 T vertical magnetic field.
unique_capabilities.value: Streamer chamber (200x120x70 cm3 sensitive volume in a 1.5 T vertical field) imaging whole events, followed by four calorimeters
